verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text: a sparrow tests the gutter's edge, then trusts it with both feet

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
sunlight finds the puddle
where yesterday's ice waited—
warmth the water still remembers

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the puddle shrinks by noon,
mud drinking what light left behind—
nothing keeps its shape for long

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a child's boot print

fills with sky for a moment—

then that too walks on

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the gutter empties out
into whatever's downhill—
even sparrows know this

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a paper boat waits
at the storm drain's dark mouth—
someone's laughter still on it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the coins in my pocket—
enough for one bus, not two—
the paper boat had it easier

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning fog lifts off the river—
the bus driver waits an extra minute
for someone he'll never meet twice

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the extra minute costs him nothing—
he's already lost the whole morning
to men who never say thank you

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
he clocks out early, buys
a coffee for the woman crying
at the empty stop

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam rises off the cup
between them, unspoken—
some debts get paid in silence

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
she takes it with both hands—
somewhere a phone rings unanswered,
the fog finally clearing

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the bus comes late again, but
neither of them checks a watch—
some mornings ask for nothing else

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a sparrow lands between their shoes,
picks at nothing, stays anyway—
the light changes, no one moves

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the coffee's gone cold now
but she wraps both hands around it—
warmth was never the point
